clue.text: Food set out on plate

indicators.note: to set something out is to arrange it afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A dish being put out on a plate at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges ONPLATE. 'Set out' reads as serving the food, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, an example of a food.

clue.text: Column missing front piece of Italian stucco?

indicators.note: missing means the column word lacks a letter

parts.note: a pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall

indicators.note: front piece of picks the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: An architectural feature that has lost its Italian front decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine render for walls, an example of the material, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Where one might get a fine collection of records

definitions.text: Where one might get a fine collection of records

parts.words: Where one might get a fine collection of records
parts.note: a building of books and archives, where an overdue loan earns a fine

explanation.surface: A shop with an excellent stock of vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' means penalty, not excellent: the place both keeps records and charges late fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A public lending institution holds collected written records and fines borrowers for late returns.

clue.text: Female, Type A

parts.note: the norm is the standard type or pattern

explanation.surface: A woman described as a Type A personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Willing daughter stops being open to possible change

indicators.note: stops as in plugs a gap, so the daughter goes into the middle

parts.note: amenable means willing or cooperative

explanation.surface: A cooperative daughter ceases being open to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like ceasing but means filling a hole: D plugs AMENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: If a law or text can be revised, it can be altered by amendment.

clue.text: Showing little humour, people often initially rejected weaker coffee

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words people and often
something rejected is sent back, so the coffee word is read backwards

parts.note: decaf is coffee without its caffeine, so a weaker brew

explanation.surface: Grumpy customers sending back a feeble coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sounds like the customers refusing the drink, but it reverses the coffee word; 'Showing little humour' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone po-faced keeps a stern, disapproving expression and shows no amusement.

clue.text: Visit American relative at home

parts.note: pop is American for father
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Calling on an American dad at his house.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop in is to make a short, informal call on someone.

clue.text: Cheap ornament is cool to hang

parts.note: to fan is to cool with moving air
to dangle is to hang loosely

explanation.surface: A cheap decoration that looks cool when hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandangle is a showy trinket or gaudy decoration of little value.

clue.text: Fancy ring given to a king on retirement

parts.note: to chime is to ring like a bell

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so these letters run backwards in a down clue

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An elaborate ring presented to a monarch when he steps down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns AR round to give RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fancy, a fanciful dream or illusion.

clue.text: Head of family put away small gifts

definitions.note: verb, third person, as in he gifts

parts.note: a don is the head of a Mafia family
to put food away is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: The family patriarch packing away little presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To gift something is to give it freely, as a charitable donor does.

clue.text: Taxi service housed by a grand European hotel

indicators.note: a thing housed by another sits within it, so the taxi firm goes inside the other letters

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
Uber is a ride-hailing taxi company

explanation.surface: A cab firm's base inside a smart continental hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, a simple country hotel or guest house.

clue.text: Money saved up for foreign holiday property

definitions.meaning: the retirement fund someone builds over their working life
a ... in France or Spain is a boarding house or small guest house

explanation.surface: Using retirement savings to buy a villa abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a retirement income fund and a continental boarding house.

clue.text: A great new place to study and somewhere to eat

indicators.note: new letters come from making the word over afresh, a fresh arrangement of the two words

parts.note: a den is a private room for work or study

explanation.surface: A great new study space with a café attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AGREAT into TEAGAR, followed by DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Spy acts oddly without information

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the odd letters wrap around the information word
oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word acts

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy behaving strangely with nothing to report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking information, but in its old sense it means outside, so the odd letters wrap round the information word.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is an operative who gathers intelligence, a spy.

clue.text: Poem of Frost broadcast on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the frost word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, ice crystals on surfaces

explanation.surface: A Robert Frost poem being read out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost, but it is just frozen dew, RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme is a short verse, as in a nursery rhyme, so a kind of poem.

clue.text: Rioting is to come closer to Milton Keynes?

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order
the closer of a word is its final letter, here of Milton

explanation.surface: Riots approaching the new town of Milton Keynes.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is an English new town; split up, Keynes becomes the economist John Maynard Keynes.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was a famous British economist, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Downbeat artist's gripped by good southern country music

parts.note: downbeat means gloomy or sad, which is blue

indicators.note: a thing gripped by others is held between them, so the artist goes inside

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist; with the 's it gives RAS

explanation.surface: A gloomy painter clutching a fine Southern folk tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a style of American country music from Kentucky, played on banjo and fiddle.

clue.text: Complete opportunity to disregard children, it's said

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for something spoken

parts.note: utter means complete or total

indicators.note: to disregard is to leave out, so the children letters are removed

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: A rare chance to ignore the kids, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' looks like a homophone signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is a spoken word or remark, something voiced.

clue.text: Shy person beginning to get, for the most part, really tense

parts.note: an intro is the opening part of something

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: really and very both intensify, as in really good
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A timid person who is very tense at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of VERY to leave VER; 'to get' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is someone reserved and inward-looking, typically a quiet, retiring sort.

clue.text: Superhero name adopted by one Italian

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the name letter goes inside

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome

explanation.surface: An Italian taking on a hero's alias.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Man is a Marvel comics character, an armoured superhero.

clue.text: Much-revered thing a singer does on stage?

definitions.meaning: held in deep reverence, like a sacred emblem

definitions.text: thing a singer does on stage?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., carrying the microphone around

explanation.surface: A singer's revered on-stage routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something totemic is treated as a sacred symbol, venerated by a group.

clue.text: Was liable to miss the opening over

indicators.note: missing the opening means losing the first letter of the phrase

parts.note: tended means was inclined or apt to

explanation.surface: Someone prone to missing the start of a cricket over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is an adjective here, finished, not the cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over is finished or complete, at its close.

clue.text: Within two days, odd bits of ice have to subside

indicators.note: within puts the odd letters of ice between the two days

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two of them

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in odd positions of the word ice

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Ice melting away over a couple of days.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to lessen in strength and fade away.

clue.text: A number of people possibly sit and tend to shift about

indicators.note: to shift letters about is to move them into a new order

explanation.surface: Crowds sitting and fidgeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' reads as a count but means one who numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist numbs patients with anaesthetic, so they make people go numb.

clue.text: Excel is known to work

parts.note: a secret that is out has become known
do means work, as in that will do the job

explanation.surface: The Microsoft spreadsheet program is known to function.
explanation.walkthrough: Excel is not the software here but the verb, to be better than.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel over others is to surpass them, beat them at their own game.

clue.text: I book transportation first, then head out of Jamaica?

indicators.note: first puts the transport word at the front of the answer
then signals the next piece follows on behind

parts.note: a car is a form of transport
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Booking a car first and then heading out of Jamaica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as leaving, but it means originating from.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica is an island in the Caribbean Sea, so its people and things are from that region.

clue.text: Class project supported by headteacher at the halfway point

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below

parts.note: to cast is to project or throw

indicators.note: the halfway point is the central letter of headteacher

explanation.surface: A school project backed by the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a fixed hereditary social class, as in India.

clue.text: Large, extremely hot section of Australia's coastline

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: extremely picks the outermost letters of the word hot

explanation.surface: A vast, scorching stretch of the Australian shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Australian Bight is a wide bay along the southern coast, a curve of shore.

clue.text: Records of note provided by US tax officers

parts.note: a memo is a brief written note
the IRS, Internal Revenue Service, collects US federal taxes

explanation.surface: Notable documents supplied by American taxmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoirs are written accounts of one's life and experiences, a kind of personal record.

clue.text: Cocktail is 50% neat rum or gin

indicators.note: 50% means half of the word, its first two letters
rum means odd or strange, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink half of neat rum or gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a spirit but is the anagram signal, turning ORGIN into GRONI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Negroni is a mixed drink of gin, vermouth and Campari.

clue.text: Clothing and drink reportedly coming from south-east Asia?

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the Asian word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Thai means from Thailand, in south-east Asia

explanation.surface: Clothes and drinks imported from south-east Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a garment worn knotted at the collar, an item of clothing.

clue.text: No more money held by former heads of city trading

indicators.note: something held by other letters sits between them

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: heads of picks the opening letters of city and trading

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: No more cash left in the hands of former financial district traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct has died out and exists no longer.
